aiOverview.content: As of March 2026, COVID-19 symptoms in the US are heavily influenced by new, highly mutated Omicron subvariants such as BA.3.2 (nicknamed "Cicada") and Stratus, which are causing a rise in cases. These variants are known to evade immunity from earlier infections and vaccines, with BA.3.2 specifically noted for having 70-75 mutations in its spike protein. Top COVID-19 Symptoms in 2026:The 2026 variants predominantly cause upper respiratory symptoms, often described as feeling like a severe cold or flu. Common symptoms include: Severe Sore Throat: Frequently described as "razorblade throat" or sharp, intense pain. Congestion and Runny Nose: High reports of sinus pressure and congestion. Fatigue and Weakness: Intense tiredness. Dry Cough: Persistent cough. Headache and Body Aches. Hoarseness/Raspy Voice: Specifically noted with the "Stratus" variant. Fever or Chills. Loss of Smell or Taste: Still reported, though less common than in earlier pandemic years. Key Trends in 2026: Immune Escape: The new variants are adept at evading protection from previous vaccines, although the 2025-2026 vaccines (targeting the JN.1 lineage) are still expected to offer protection against severe disease. Similar to Cold/Flu: It is increasingly difficult to distinguish COVID-19 from other respiratory viruses without testing. Duration: Most people recover in 5-10 days, though cough and fatigue can persist, especially in older adults. When to Seek Care: Immediate medical attention is recommended if you experience severe shortness of breath, persistent chest pain, confusion, or bluish lips. Disclaimer: Symptoms can vary from person to person. Testing is the most reliable way to confirm a COVID-19 infection, and rapid tests are still effective for these new variants.
